beats.t: By morning, the library had fallen quiet as though it had never been wet. Dried books lay open in rows on every reading desk beneath the domed ceiling.
One hundred and twelve books. Pig, what kind of place makes a chef dry books?
Thanks for your hard work. Five stars, plus an ironing service.
Pay me in food, not stars. Can't eat stars.
With each ember Moka rolled, the damp pages unfurled softly. Something like the scent of warm bread rose from them.
Lovely smell. It must be a book about someone's birthday morning.
You can tell that from how a book smells?
No, I just said it. Sounded convincing, didn't it?
See? A con artist starts scamming first thing in the morning.
And Mr. Otter starts remembering me first thing. Thank you.
Don't put it like that. I can't even get mad.
The baby dragon wriggled off Yeoni's wrist. Its belly was round and swollen, and tiny droplets flew out whenever it yawned.
Look at this one. Still digesting yesterday's flood.
If a dragon gets an upset stomach from drinking water, what kind of weather is that? Monsoon?
A storehouse that isn't full is good news. It means it can drink the next flood, too.
Hear that? You're our team's official water purifier.
Apparently pleased, the baby dragon curled its tail once around Yeoni's hoof and fell asleep again.
At the end of the desk, Yeoni opened their hoof. The eight-slot chart appeared. Seven spaces were filled, one of them frozen black.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
(Only one left. But where do I find this blank?)
Yundal. The first character of the Hour Pillar. What belongs here?
With an Eul Wood Day Master, Gyeong Metal belongs there. The place of Influence.
What's Influence? One line, please.
Energy that governs and protects you. Like rules, or a name tag.
We found all the others on islands. I've never seen an Island of Influence.
No chart is without Influence. If you can't see it, it's hiding.
She remembered the mist over the river that first night, and the lights rising beyond it one by one.
(Yeongnyangi said my characters were scattered across four islands.)
Blue light, flickering firelight, golden light, and a light like old bookshelves. There had definitely been four.
There were four lights. But the Ten Gods have five branches. One whole branch is empty.
You've been studying, my lady. Care for a part-time job at my compatibility booth?
That's not what we're talking about.
Where'd the fifth light go, then? Someone pocket it?
I don't know how to find it either. People with empty hours don't usually stare at that space for long.
You said it protects me. Then that space should react strongest when I'm in danger.
My lady, that expression is a little frightening.
(If I want to know who protects me, I can make something need protecting.)
Then the reading room door opened. Yeongnyangi came in. His fur was half dry, and he hesitated very slightly with each step on his left paw.
Yeongnyangi, you said four islands at first. Where's the fifth?
There isn't one now.
Only one of the five branches is missing? Does that make sense?
Customer Support is closed.
Say that once more and I'll actually file it.
Yeongnyangi sat at the far end of the desk. Normally, he would have sat beside Yeoni. Yeoni glanced at that empty place.
(He's been like this since yesterday. Every time I move closer, he steps back.)
Mr. Cat, may I ask when your birthday is?
Why?
I ask everyone I meet. Especially someone always beside you, my lady.
I don't know.
You don't know. Interesting in itself.
Fraud, you're sounding the cat out. Even I can see that.
Walking between desks, Yeoni stopped before a wheeled ladder at the end of the reading room. It reached the ceiling shelves.
I'm trying an experiment. Moka, put out your fire. Yundal, stand beneath the ladder.
What now? Pig experiments usually end with me getting hurt.
She told Yeongnyangi nothing. At the far end, he was shaking out his wet hat.
My hour is empty too. If I stand below, I'll muddle your experiment.
That's why I'm asking. I'm measuring both of you.
She climbed to the top. Five petals trembled on her head. The one faded white on the first day shook first.
At the top rung she took a breath and let go with both forelegs. She deliberately kept the vines wound inside her wrists.
Yundal hooked the nape of her neck with his folding umbrella's handle. The empty space shivered once; the handle slipped under her weight.
Something white sprang from the far end. As Yeongnyangi hurled himself beneath her, the empty space flared white like sunlight on cold metal.
They rolled together onto a pile of books. Her left hind leg caught on the ladder and bent the wrong way.
Ow. Did you see? Once for Yundal, once for you.
Show me your hind leg.
It's fine. Doesn't hurt as much as I thought.
When did you pile up those books?
This morning. I said I was drying them, and stacked them myself.
Yeongnyangi's ears slowly flattened. He looked at the books beneath the ladder, Yundal's umbrella, and the vines still wound tightly around her wrists.
You fell on purpose?
I wanted to know who would react. Everyone keeps saying later.
So you tested me. With your own leg at stake.
Moka's flame shrank. No one here had ever seen Yeongnyangi raise his voice.
What if I hadn't caught you?
But you did.
Never do it again. Next time I won't catch you.
He turned and left the reading room. Behind the dragging sound of his left paw, the door slammed unusually hard.
Hey. The cat can shout? Much scarier than when he's being obnoxious.
I didn't know either. That he could speak that loudly.
Yundal tied his umbrella to his bag again and crouched by her hind leg. His gloved fingers pressed the swollen ankle twice.
Sprained. You'll limp for three days.
It shook for you too. What was that?
I told you my hour is empty. Empty spaces greeting each other.
Quite bright for a greeting.
Both looked bright to me. The cat's was a little whiter.
Influence has another meaning in a woman's chart. I'll tell you when your ankle heals.
All afternoon, Yeoni limped through the library. Grumbling, Moka wound bookmark ribbons around her ankle.
If we don't know, we can look it up. Let's try the catalog desk.
That chatty card cabinet from the first day? It's the one that told me to be quiet.
The catalog desk's drawers rattled open as soon as they saw the pair. One card flew out and stopped before Yeoni's nose.
[ Please state your search terms · Borrowing allowance: 0/1 ]
Flower pig, Influence, fifth light.
The letters on the card bled like ink, then gathered again. Only one line came back.
[ No results · Location: Outside the library · Contact: Customer Support ]
Customer Support?
What's Customer Support? They have that here?
There is. Customer service that accepts neither complaints nor worries.
Yeoni turned the card over. A faint pawprint marked one back corner.
That's the cat's paw. He keeps putting it on my skewers. I know the size.
(Someone searched before me. With this same card.)
Moka. Is there anything about Yeongnyangi you haven't told me?
Nope. Otters don't know secrets.
Your tail is wagging incredibly fast.
I'm drying my fur! It got wet drying the books!
Moka hurried off toward another shelf. Yeoni watched him go for a long time.
(Three days. I can't even run after a cat who keeps leaving until then.)
That night, everyone slept in a little room deep in the library. Moka snored with a book for a pillow.
(Can't sleep. My ankle and that empty space both keep aching.)
Tossing and turning, Yeoni looked toward the corner. The spot where Yeongnyangi always curled up to sleep was empty.
Yeongnyangi?
No answer. Yeoni pushed back the blanket and sat up. Between Moka's snores, they could hear their own heartbeat.
A few strands of white fur and a note lay in the empty spot. A pawprint served as a signature.
[ Back soon. Worries not accepted. · Customer Support ]
What kind of note is this? Why won't you accept worries?!
(He gets that angry all day, then leaves one note.)
Yeoni rose with the note, stepped on her injured leg, and sat straight back down. The baby dragon on her wrist opened sleepy eyes and turned toward the window.
Rain sounded outside. The sky was clear, but the smell of rain was there.
I know that smell.
(The same smell as the flooded shelves and the chains. A wet cloak.)
She folded the note into her hoof and hopped to the window. Pressing her forehead to the glass, she could see outside.
A half-eaten sun hung in the night sky. Two shadows stood atop a round roof.
One was a white cat in a hat. The other, a black tiger with rain dripping from her cloak.
They weren't fighting. They stood a little apart, looking toward the same stretch of sky.
Why are they together?
The baby dragon bit down hard on Yeoni's hoof. Whether it meant don't go or hurry, Yeoni couldn't tell.
Okay, I'll be quiet. You hold your breath too.
She hooked a foreleg over the window frame, then stopped. She couldn't climb that rounded roof on a sprained hind leg.
The character board floated above her hoof by itself. Inside the space that had blazed white that afternoon was an unfamiliar stroke.
(That stroke wasn't there earlier.)
Someone stirred behind her. Yundal, whom she'd thought asleep, sat with his folding umbrella on his knees, watching her empty space in the dark.
